engines.name: AutoResearchClaw
engines.role: Optional external research pipeline; reference for citation identity checks, experiment repair and numeric provenance.
engines.code_license: MIT; uninspected bundled components retain separate terms.
engines.weights_terms: No mandatory weights identified; chosen LLMs/models have independent terms.
engines.data_service_terms: Configured LLM/ACP and scholarly providers may receive prompts, queries and artifacts; provider subscription/API and compute costs apply.
prerequisites: Separately installed Python >=3.11 environment and selected upstream configuration.
Authorized LLM/ACP backend, provider terms and explicit spending/compute/storage bounds.
Task-specific experiment dependencies; LaTeX for applicable local compilation.
engines.inputs: Research topic/configuration, source records and experiment artifacts.
engines.outputs: Pipeline artifacts, manuscript drafts, verification reports and run records; depends on configuration.
limitations: Reference and optional external installation; no automatic agent setup, memory injection, execution or publishing.
Global numeric matching is not condition-specific claim entailment; identity-resolved citations do not prove sentence support.
Preserve failed/negative runs and disclose selection; current source revision is not installed-version evidence.

engines.name: Beeblio
engines.role: Reference-only local research workspace patterns: bibliography, literature matrix and source-tagged search.
engines.code_license: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; restricted permitted use and distribution notices.
engines.weights_terms: No mandatory weights identified; configured model/provider terms are separate.
engines.data_service_terms: OpenRouter and scholarly APIs receive selected data; optional public sharing and Office previews add data destinations and costs.
prerequisites: Reference-only integration; do not copy upstream implementation into a commercial-capable skill.
Any separate app installation requires compatible Node 24/pnpm 11, Python/Bash and configured provider access.
Resolve package repository-name discrepancy before installation.
engines.inputs: Research workspace files, bibliography identities, literature queries and local datasets.
engines.outputs: Bibliography records, comparison matrix, derived analysis files and reports.
limitations: Not a mandatory dependency or bundled app; no verified general-purpose scientific CLI.
Local shell inherits environment and is not constrained to project by ordinary file-path checks.
Do not enable sharing/tunnels or transmit previews automatically; keep project notes separate from global memory.

engines.name: AlphaFold 3
engines.role: Biomolecular structure/complex prediction for proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands and supported modifications.
engines.code_license: Apache-2.0 source; third-party dependencies retain their terms.
engines.weights_terms: Custom terms: Google-direct weights; noncommercial use by/on behalf of noncommercial organizations; restricted weight sharing and output distribution/training uses.
engines.data_service_terms: Output terms require notices, modification disclosure and citation. Databases have separate attribution/CC0/other terms. Server and Google Cloud routes have separate terms, accounts and costs.
prerequisites: Compatible Python >=3.12 environment, compiled dependencies and licensed Google-provided weights.
Prepared JSON matching pinned parser, CCD/custom chemistry and required MSAs/templates/databases.
Documented Linux/NVIDIA route; current code also exposes CPU/MPS with XLA attention, requiring environment-specific validation.
Full search installation: approximately 252 GB compressed databases/up to 1 TB installed; RAM/device/runtime budget must be checked.
engines.inputs: AlphaFold JSON dialect versions 1–4: sequences, seeds, optional MSAs/templates, CCD/SMILES ligands and supported bonded atoms/custom CCD.
engines.outputs: Predicted mmCIF structures, confidence/summary JSON, ranking data, processed inputs and terms files.
limitations: Executable placeholder is the user-supplied run_alphafold.py path; recipe requires its compatible environment.
Installation prose says Linux/GPU; current source supports --jax_backend=cpu|mps with --flash_attention_implementation=xla. Neither alternate route is validated by this catalog.
GPU and CPU preparation can be split; missing fields may trigger substantial search.
Modifications use 1-based positions; arbitrary chemistry needs compatible CCD/conformers/topology.
Predicted confidence/structure does not establish function, binding or experimental validation; commercial server terms do not follow Apache licensing.

engines.name: Boltz
engines.role: Biomolecular complex structure prediction; Boltz-2 optionally estimates protein–small-molecule affinity.
engines.weights_terms: Upstream README explicitly licenses code and model weights MIT for academic/commercial use.
engines.data_service_terms: MSA server/data terms are independent; --use_msa_server submits sequences externally and can require authentication. Local prepared MSAs avoid that route.
prerequisites: Separate compatible Python >=3.10,<3.13/PyTorch environment and preprovisioned checkpoints/CCD assets.
YAML inputs with local MSAs or explicitly chosen single-sequence mode.
Selected CPU/GPU runtime, storage and time budget; CPU is documented but slow.
engines.inputs: YAML biomolecule/chain declarations, ligand SMILES or CCD, optional modifications/templates/constraints and affinity property request.
engines.outputs: Ranked mmCIF/PDB poses, confidence JSON and NPZ arrays; optional affinity JSON.
limitations: Entry is a CPU prepared-MSA recipe; it does not prove local availability or forbid a separately validated GPU route.
Startup downloads missing checkpoints/assets; preflight those dependencies before execution and do not add MSA upload automatically.
Modified positions are 1-based; covalent/chemical support is restricted.
Affinity targets one small-molecule ligand against protein; RNA/DNA/cofactor targets are unreliable. log10(IC50 in micromolar) and binder probability are predictions, not measured Kd/free energy.
No audited native macOS MPS or universal RAM/VRAM guarantee.

engines.name: Meta ESM / fair-esm
engines.role: Protein embeddings/contact and variant scores; ESMFold protein folding; ESM-IF1 inverse folding.
engines.weights_terms: Separate checkpoint-specific terms not located in bounded repository audit; record exact checkpoint provenance and terms before use.
engines.data_service_terms: Atlas data is CC BY 4.0 with linked Meta terms; other datasets/services are separate. Historical Atlas API availability and terms were not verified.
prerequisites: Separate fair-esm environment; do not coinstall Biohub esm in its Python namespace.
Trusted preprovisioned selected checkpoints and compatible PyTorch.
Native ESMFold installation has older Python <=3.9/OpenFold/nvcc requirements despite CPU inference flags; check per task.
engines.inputs: FASTA sequences for embeddings/folding; protein backbone PDB/mmCIF for inverse-folding APIs/scripts.
engines.outputs: Per-sequence .pt representations/contact data, PDB structures, sequence designs or conditional likelihood CSV depending on interface.
limitations: Example uses esm-extract; folding and inverse-folding need different interfaces and prerequisites.
Archived repository; documented hosted endpoints are not current availability evidence.
Extractor truncation/batching must be recorded; .pt checkpoint/artifact provenance must be trusted.
Protein/multimer folding is not general ligand/cofactor/DNA/RNA chemistry. Scores and generated sequences do not validate function.

engines.name: Biohub ESM
engines.role: ESMC sequence representations, ESM3 multimodal generation and ESMFold2 all-atom biomolecular complex prediction.
engines.code_license: MIT source; separately licensed dependencies in third-party notices.
engines.weights_terms: Current upstream and official ESMFold2/ESM3-small weight cards indicate MIT; ESMC-6B metadata is MIT plus other/third-party notices. Pin actual checkpoint and inspect associated terms.
engines.data_service_terms: Model cards refer to Biohub acceptable-use policy. Hosted API requires token and independent service/privacy/cost review; training data rights do not follow code license.
prerequisites: Separate Biohub esm environment, distinct from fair-esm; Python >=3.12 and compatible PyTorch 2.11 stack.
Preprovisioned selected model/backbone/tokenizer/CCD files with terms, hashes and storage budget.
Match CPU/CUDA/ROCm/MPS capabilities to each model and kernels; documented folding example uses CUDA.
Typed structure inputs with compatible molecular chemistry; explicit authorization for any hosted route.
engines.inputs: ESMC tokenized protein sequences; ESM3 partial sequence/structure/function tracks; ESMFold2 typed protein/DNA/RNA/ligand/MSA/modification inputs.
engines.outputs: Logits/embeddings/hidden states; generated protein tracks/PDB; or all-atom mmCIF and confidence arrays.
limitations: Python APIs are verified; no general scientific CLI invented.
Default package is already several GB; model weights/backbone/cache add more. No universal VRAM/RAM estimate established.
Current source exposes CPU loading, which does not itself prove CPU folding. README esm[gpu] extras and inspected pyproject disagree.
ESMFold2 modification positions are zero-based; modification SMILES is TODO; chainbreaks and covalent bonds have compatibility limits.
Larger hosted ESM3 availability differs from local small-open model. Predictions/function labels are hypotheses, not validated biology.

engines.name: OpenMM
engines.role: Molecular simulation engine: forces, energies, integration, states and trajectories; Reference-platform toy check is a diagnostic.
engines.code_license: API/Reference/CPU MIT; CUDA/OpenCL LGPL; other components have additional notices.
engines.weights_terms: No pretrained weights required for classical toy energy; ML plugins/models have independent terms.
engines.data_service_terms: Force fields, parameters, input structures and plugins have independent provenance/terms; no service needed for a basic local toy calculation.
prerequisites: Compatible OpenMM build and selected available platform; choose Reference explicitly for the toy check.
Real simulations additionally need topology, positions, force-field parameters, units and a scientifically justified protocol.
Set RAM/runtime/trajectory/checkpoint storage budgets; test backend availability in the selected environment.
engines.inputs: Toy particles/force constants or prepared molecular topology, positions, parameters and simulation protocol.
engines.outputs: Potential energies with units, states, trajectories, checkpoints and simulation logs depending on API.
limitations: Verified Python API, not a general single-file simulation CLI.
MIT does not cover every backend/component; installed backend availability is not universal OS/GPU support.
Toy energy success does not validate MD, equilibrium sampling, binding affinity or experimental mechanism.
Noncanonical residues/cofactors need compatible topology/force-field parameters; do not silently substitute.

engines.name: RDKit
engines.role: CPU cheminformatics: molecular parsing, descriptors, fingerprints, conformers and force-field optimization.
engines.code_license: BSD-3-Clause; bundled components retain their notices.
engines.weights_terms: No pretrained weights needed for basic descriptors or conformers.
engines.data_service_terms: No external service/dataset needed for basic local operations; input and external data rights remain separate.
prerequisites: Compatible isolated RDKit environment and CPU; select current supported wheel/conda build.
Explicit SMILES/stereochemistry/charge/fragment interpretation; seeded conformer settings and supported force field.
User-selected artifact paths and time/output bounds.
engines.inputs: SMILES or supported molecular structure data plus descriptor/conformer options.
engines.outputs: Descriptor records, fingerprints, molecular structures/SDF conformers and explicit optimizer status/provenance.
limitations: Verified Python APIs; this skill's descriptors/conformer commands are original wrappers.
Reject invalid/empty inputs and nonfinite outputs; distinguish embedding failure and nonconverged optimization.
Do not silently substitute force fields or assume parameters exist for metals/noncanonical chemistry.
Descriptors and minimized conformers do not prove measured solubility, potency, safety or bound geometry.

engines.name: DeepChem
engines.role: Molecular/materials ML featurization, datasets, model training, predictions and evaluation.
engines.weights_terms: Checkpoint-specific terms must be checked; code licensing does not clear pretrained models.
engines.data_service_terms: MoleculeNet and other datasets/services have independent licenses and download/privacy costs; example loaders can fetch data.
prerequisites: Separate compatible environment and selected backend; README/Python metadata ranges differ.
Backend-specific versions (Torch/JAX/TensorFlow) and accelerator support checked independently.
Authorized labeled data/checkpoints with provenance, split/leakage checks and runtime/storage budget.
engines.inputs: Molecular/materials data and labels, featurizer, model and explicit evaluation configuration.
engines.outputs: Feature datasets, trained checkpoints, predictions and metric dictionaries.
limitations: No verified general scientific CLI; use an explicit task-specific Python workflow.
CPU featurization/classical models are possible; native Apple GPU support is not established.
Current dependency pins can conflict with other engines; do not combine environments by default.
Dataset download examples are not offline smoke checks; benchmark metrics do not establish assay performance or applicability-domain validity.

engines.name: DiffDock
engines.role: Protein–small-molecule docking pose prediction and confidence ranking; current default is DiffDock-L.
engines.weights_terms: README explicitly applies MIT to code and DiffDock model weights; ESM/OpenFold dependencies have separate provenance/terms.
engines.data_service_terms: Protein/ligand and benchmark data, public demos and cloud GPU services retain separate terms. Do not upload private structures automatically.
prerequisites: Compatible separately provisioned repository environment; supplied Python3.9/CUDA11.7 stack is not a native Apple Silicon recipe.
Preprovisioned pinned DiffDock/ESM assets and caches; prevent uncapped startup downloads.
Prepared protein PDB and ligand/CSV; PDB CPU route documented, GPU faster; sequence route adds ESMFold.
Explicit working directory/module path, model hashes and runtime/storage/network budget.
engines.inputs: CSV fields complex_name, protein_path, ligand_description, protein_sequence; protein PDB/sequence and ligand SMILES or supported file.
engines.outputs: Ranked SDF poses with confidence values; optional reverse-process visualization.
limitations: Recipe requires compatible checkout/module path and reviewed configuration.
Missing weights can trigger automatic ZIP fetch/extraction; model archive is only part of total storage.
Protein-small-molecule domain; confidence is not binding affinity or experimental validation.
Preparation, receptor conformation and distribution shifts can invalidate pose interpretation.

engines.name: REINVENT4
engines.role: Generative molecular design: sampling, transfer/reinforcement learning, scaffold/linker/R-group tasks.
engines.weights_terms: Separately hosted prior-model license/version/hash/size remained unverified because linked Zenodo record was inaccessible; obtain explicit provenance before use.
engines.data_service_terms: Optional scoring programs/services and datasets have independent terms; OpenEye ROCS requires separate toolkit/license. Set external spending bounds.
prerequisites: Separate compatible Python >=3.11 environment; current source Torch/RDKit/numpy pins differ from other engines.
User-provided compatible prior/checkpoint with verified terms and explicit TOML/JSON/YAML config.
CPU fallback documented; Linux validated upstream, macOS support depends on appropriate PyTorch/MPS build.
Runtime/model/cache/storage budgets; GPU recommended for training.
engines.inputs: Configuration naming task/mode, model file, device, sample count, output and optional reference/scaffold/fragment SMILES.
engines.outputs: Sampled SMILES/negative log-likelihood CSV; training agents, scoring outputs and logs depend on mode/config.
limitations: Output placeholder here is log path; scientific output paths are explicit fields inside the input config.
Do not run CUDA-oriented uv defaults blindly on another platform.
README-named prior_registry.py was absent at audited revision; use verified explicit model-path config.
High scores/valid SMILES do not establish activity, safety, synthesizability or real-world novelty.

engines.name: Open Babel
engines.role: Chemical format conversion, search/filtering and coordinate-generation toolkit.
engines.code_license: GPL-2.0-only in package metadata; COPYING GPLv2; no binaries bundled by this catalog.
engines.weights_terms: No neural weights needed for basic conversion.
engines.data_service_terms: No online service needed for basic local conversion; input-data rights and build-time dependency/download terms remain separate.
prerequisites: User-supplied compatible executable or Python bindings; CPU is sufficient.
Explicit input/output formats, destination and identity/charge/stereochemistry checks.
Build dependencies and possible auto-downloads reviewed if installing separately.
engines.inputs: Supported molecular files or SMILES plus format/conversion options.
engines.outputs: Converted molecular files or generated coordinates, with possible information loss.
limitations: Example explicitly converts SMILES file to SDF; it does not promise 3D coordinates.
Conversion may change aromaticity, bonds, hydrogens, charge, fragments or unsupported fields; validate relevant identity before/after.
Generic Open Babel build is not necessarily GNINA's recommended fork/version.
Generated coordinates are model geometries, not experimental structures.

engines.name: GNINA
engines.role: Docking, pose optimization and empirical/CNN scoring for protein–ligand systems.
engines.code_license: GPL/Apache conditions: supplied Open Babel integration forces GPL; Apache-only use requires removing Open Babel references. Not an ordinary Apache-only binary.
engines.weights_terms: Bundled model files are present, but separate per-weight licenses were not located; inspect exact models and any external downloads.
engines.data_service_terms: CrossDocked/DUD-E and other training/benchmark datasets or model repositories have separate unverified terms; remote GPU/compute costs need a budget.
prerequisites: User-supplied compatible Linux/WSL binary/environment; native macOS execution not established.
Prepared receptor PDB, ligand SDF, binding-site/autobox definition, model identity and explicit bounded search settings.
Current source build requires CUDA>=12 even though runtime --no_gpu exists.
Prebuilt binary alone can be about 2 GB; check full download/build/runtime/output budgets.
engines.inputs: Receptor PDB, ligand SDF and box coordinates/sizes or reference ligand; optional scoring/minimization/search configuration.
engines.outputs: Ranked ligand poses, empirical/CNN score fields and logs.
limitations: No general one-input command template: receptor, ligand and search-site mapping require an explicit task plan.
--no_gpu is runtime CPU selection, not proof of CUDA-free source build or Apple GPU support.
CNNscore, CNNaffinity and empirical energy are distinct; do not rename them one confidence/affinity metric.
Docking scores/poses are computational hypotheses; protonation, waters/metals, stereochemistry, controls and physical validity matter.
